grades.calculation.other.weighted.title: Grading System: Weighted
grades.calculation.other.weighted.where: Grades > Settings > Calculation Options > Grading System
grades.calculation.other.weighted.what: Each category and item carries a percentage of the final grade, and those percentages add up to 100. A 25% exam counts for a quarter of the course no matter how many points it is marked out of.
grades.calculation.other.weighted.when: The syllabus is written in percentages: 'Homework 30%, Midterm 30%, Final 40%'. This is the most common choice at MSU.

options.label: Weighted
options.effect: Percentages decide the final grade. Points out of are only used within a category.

options.label: Points
options.effect: Points decide everything. Any weights you typed are ignored.

options.label: Formula
options.effect: A custom expression decides the final grade.

grades.calculation.other.weighted.learnerSees: In their grades, each category shows its own subtotal and the weight it carries.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings.
Choose the Calculation Options tab.
Select Weighted under Grading System.
Click Save, and confirm the two prompts D2L raises.
grades.calculation.other.weighted.verify: Open Manage Grades: the Weight column should be editable and the category weights should total 100.
gotchas: Weights that do not total 100 still calculate, but not the way the professor expects. Manage Grades warns about this.
Switching system after grading is entered changes every final grade in the course. Warn the professor before they confirm.
A category's items are weighted relative to each other inside the category, not against the whole course.
tickets: "My students' final grades are all wrong after I set up weights."
"The syllabus says the midterm is 30% but D2L shows something else."
grades.calculation.other.weighted.msu: Observed in the Same Playground sandbox on 2026-09-22.

grades.calculation.other.points.title: Grading System: Points
grades.calculation.other.points.where: Grades > Settings > Calculation Options > Grading System
grades.calculation.other.points.what: The final grade is earned points divided by total possible points. A 200-point final naturally counts twice as much as a 100-point midterm, with no percentages involved.
grades.calculation.other.points.when: The syllabus is written in points: 'the course is out of 1000 points'.

options.label: Points
options.effect: Point totals alone decide the final grade.

options.label: Weighted
options.effect: Percentages decide it instead, and point totals only matter within a category.

grades.calculation.other.points.learnerSees: Their final grade as points earned out of points possible.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings.
Choose the Calculation Options tab.
Select Points under Grading System.
Click Save and confirm.
grades.calculation.other.points.verify: In Manage Grades the Weight column is no longer in play; check that Max. Points on each item matches the syllabus.
gotchas: Weight values entered earlier are ignored, not deleted. Switching back to Weighted brings them back and can surprise people.
To make an item count more, raise its Max. Points. There is no weight to adjust.
tickets: "I set weights but they are not doing anything."
"How do I make the final exam worth more?"

grades.calculation.other.formula-referen.title: Grading System: Formula
grades.calculation.other.formula-referen.where: Grades > Settings > Calculation Options > Grading System
grades.calculation.other.formula-referen.what: The final grade comes from a custom expression the professor writes, which can do things weights and points cannot, such as 'drop the lowest two quizzes, but only if the final exam is above 60'.
grades.calculation.other.formula-referen.when: Rarely. Escalate rather than improvise: a wrong formula silently produces wrong grades for the whole class.
grades.calculation.other.formula-referen.learnerSees: A final grade with no visible explanation of how it was reached, which generates its own tickets.
howTo: Treat this as an escalation. Record what the professor wants in plain language and pass it to a senior colleague or the D2L administrators.
grades.calculation.other.formula-referen.verify: This simulator does not evaluate formulas, so do not practise the outcome here. Confirm any real formula against a test learner in a sandbox course.
gotchas: Formula evaluation is outside this simulator's model, so the practice gradebook will not reproduce it.
Formula errors do not always announce themselves; they can just produce plausible wrong numbers.
tickets: "Can D2L drop the lowest quiz only if they passed the final?"

grades.calculation.other.exclude-ungrade.title: Ungraded items: Exclude from the final grade
grades.calculation.other.exclude-ungrade.where: Grades > Settings > Calculation Options > Ungraded Items
grades.calculation.other.exclude-ungrade.what: Work that has not been marked yet is left out of the calculation entirely. The final grade reflects only what has actually been graded so far.
grades.calculation.other.exclude-ungrade.when: Almost always during a running term. It is what a professor means by 'their grade so far'.

options.label: Exclude ungraded items
options.effect: A learner graded 90% on one of ten items shows 90%.

options.label: Treat ungraded items as 0
options.effect: The same learner shows 9%, because the nine unmarked items count as zeros.

grades.calculation.other.exclude-ungrade.learnerSees: A grade that rises and falls as work is marked, rather than starting near zero and climbing all term.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Calculation Options.
Under Ungraded Items choose Exclude.
Click Save and confirm.
grades.calculation.other.exclude-ungrade.verify: Pick a learner with one graded item and check their Final Calculated Grade matches that item alone.
gotchas: At the end of term the professor usually wants the opposite, so missing work counts as zero. Flipping this setting at the wrong moment is a common cause of panic emails.
This is a course-wide setting. To zero out one learner's single item, enter a 0 on that item instead.
tickets: "My students all think they are failing."
"Why does the gradebook say 9% when they got 90% on the only assignment?"

grades.calculation.other.treat-ungraded-.title: Ungraded items: Treat as 0
grades.calculation.other.treat-ungraded-.where: Grades > Settings > Calculation Options > Ungraded Items
grades.calculation.other.treat-ungraded-.what: Anything not yet marked counts as a zero in the final grade.
grades.calculation.other.treat-ungraded-.when: At the end of term, when unmarked work really is missing work and should pull the grade down.
grades.calculation.other.treat-ungraded-.learnerSees: Their grade drops for every item left unmarked, including work the professor simply has not got to yet.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Calculation Options.
Under Ungraded Items choose Treat as 0.
Click Save and confirm.
grades.calculation.other.treat-ungraded-.verify: Check one learner with unmarked work: their Final Calculated Grade should now be lower than before.
gotchas: Turning this on mid-term makes the whole class appear to be failing, which is one of the most common panic tickets.
It does not distinguish 'not submitted' from 'submitted but not marked yet'.
tickets: "Everyone's grade suddenly dropped and nothing changed."

grades.calculation.other.automatically-k.title: Automatically keep final grades updated
grades.calculation.other.automatically-k.where: Grades > Settings > Calculation Options > Final Grade Released
grades.calculation.other.automatically-k.what: Recalculates the final grade whenever any grade changes, instead of waiting for someone to press Recalculate.
grades.calculation.other.automatically-k.when: Leave it on in most courses. It is the reason a final grade moves as soon as a score is entered.
grades.calculation.other.automatically-k.learnerSees: Nothing directly, but a released final grade stays current rather than going stale.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Calculation Options.
Tick Automatically keep final grades updated.
Click Save.
grades.calculation.other.automatically-k.verify: Change one learner's score and confirm their Final Calculated Grade moves without any further action.
gotchas: With this off, the professor sees stale finals and assumes the gradebook is broken.
It updates the calculated grade, not the adjusted one. An adjusted final stays where it was put.
tickets: "I changed a score but the final grade did not move."

grades.calculation.other.calculated-fina.title: Final Grade Released: Calculated Final Grade
grades.calculation.other.calculated-fina.where: Grades > Settings > Calculation Options > Final Grade Released
grades.calculation.other.calculated-fina.what: The grade learners see is the one D2L works out from their scores. Nobody can nudge it.
grades.calculation.other.calculated-fina.when: The default, and right for most courses.

options.label: Adjusted Final Grade
options.effect: Learners see a number the professor can overwrite by hand.

grades.calculation.other.calculated-fina.learnerSees: The calculated grade, once it is released.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Calculation Options.
Under Final Grade Released choose Calculated Final Grade.
Click Save.
grades.calculation.other.calculated-fina.verify: In Enter Grades, the Final Calculated Grade column is the one that matters; the adjusted column is ignored for release.
gotchas: Releasing is separate from choosing. Picking this does not by itself show anyone their grade.
tickets: "I typed a final grade in but the student sees a different number."

grades.calculation.other.adjusted-final-.title: Final Grade Released: Adjusted Final Grade
grades.calculation.other.adjusted-final-.where: Grades > Settings > Calculation Options > Final Grade Released
grades.calculation.other.adjusted-final-.what: Learners see a final grade the professor can type over, letting them round up, apply a curve, or honour an arrangement the gradebook cannot express.
grades.calculation.other.adjusted-final-.when: The professor wants the last word on the final grade.
grades.calculation.other.adjusted-final-.learnerSees: The adjusted number, once released, not the calculated one.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Calculation Options.
Under Final Grade Released choose Adjusted Final Grade.
Click Save.
In Enter Grades, use Transfer calculated to adjusted to seed the column, then edit individual learners.
grades.calculation.other.adjusted-final-.verify: Change an adjusted value for one learner and confirm the learner view shows the adjusted number.
gotchas: The adjusted grade does not recalculate. Once set it stays put even if scores change afterwards, which is exactly the point and exactly the trap.
An empty adjusted column means the learner sees nothing, even though their calculated grade looks fine.
tickets: "I curved the final grades but students still see the old number."
"The student's grade did not change after I fixed their quiz score."

grades.calculation.other.automatically-r.title: Automatically release final grade
grades.calculation.other.automatically-r.where: Grades > Settings > Calculation Options > Final Grade Released
grades.calculation.other.automatically-r.what: Releases each learner's final grade as soon as it is calculated, instead of the professor releasing grades deliberately.
grades.calculation.other.automatically-r.when: Courses where the running total should always be visible. Many professors prefer it off so nobody sees a partial grade.
grades.calculation.other.automatically-r.learnerSees: Their final grade at all times, including early in the term when it is based on very little.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Calculation Options.
Tick Automatically release final grade.
Click Save.
grades.calculation.other.automatically-r.verify: Open the learner view and confirm the final grade appears without any release step.
gotchas: Combined with Treat ungraded items as 0, this shows every learner a failing grade from week one.
tickets: "Students can see their final grade and I did not want that yet."

grades.calculation.other.automatically-a.title: Automatically apply a grade of zero to missing submissions
grades.calculation.other.automatically-a.what: Puts an actual 0 in the gradebook when a learner misses a due date, rather than leaving the cell blank.
grades.calculation.other.automatically-a.when: The professor wants missing work to count against learners immediately and visibly.
grades.calculation.other.automatically-a.learnerSees: A real 0 on the item, not an empty cell, so they can tell they missed something.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Calculation Options.
Tick the automatic zero option.
Click Save.
grades.calculation.other.automatically-a.verify: Check a learner who missed a due date: the item should hold 0 rather than a blank.
gotchas: This writes a real grade. Removing it later means clearing those zeros by hand.
Different from Treat ungraded items as 0, which changes the calculation without writing anything into the gradebook.
tickets: "Can D2L put in zeros automatically when students do not submit?"

grades.calculation.other.allow-calculate.title: Allow the calculated final grade to exceed 100%
grades.calculation.other.allow-calculate.what: Lets the final grade go above 100% when bonus items or generous scores push it there. With it off, the final is capped at 100%.
grades.calculation.other.allow-calculate.when: The course has bonus work and the professor wants extra credit to actually show.
grades.calculation.other.allow-calculate.learnerSees: A final above 100% where earned, instead of a capped 100%.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Calculation Options.
Tick the option to allow the final grade to exceed 100%.
Click Save.
grades.calculation.other.allow-calculate.verify: Give a learner a bonus item and confirm their final rises above 100% instead of stopping there.
gotchas: With this off, bonus points can silently do nothing for a learner already at 100%, which looks like the bonus item is broken.
tickets: "I added extra credit and nobody's grade went up."

grades.enter.other.import.title: Import grades
grades.enter.other.import.what: Brings grades in from a CSV, which is how a professor moves marks from a spreadsheet into D2L in bulk.
grades.enter.other.import.when: Marking happened outside D2L, or a publisher tool produced a spreadsheet of scores.
grades.enter.other.import.learnerSees: Nothing until the imported grades are released as usual.
howTo: Export first to get a file with the right columns and learner identifiers.
Fill in the scores in that exported file, leaving the identifier columns untouched.
Open Grades > Enter Grades > Import and upload it.
Read the preview carefully before confirming.
grades.enter.other.import.verify: Spot-check two or three learners against the spreadsheet before telling the professor it worked.
gotchas: Matching is on Org Defined ID or username, not on the learner's name. A file built by hand usually fails here.
Import is not modelled in this simulator; practise the reasoning, not the upload.
tickets: "My grade import says it cannot find the students."
"How do I get my spreadsheet of marks into D2L?"

grades.enter.other.export.title: Export grades
grades.enter.other.export.what: Downloads the gradebook as a CSV or Excel file, choosing which identifiers and which items to include.
grades.enter.other.export.when: The professor wants grades outside D2L, or needs a correctly formatted file to import back later.
howTo: Open Grades > Enter Grades > Export.
Choose the identifier the professor needs, usually Org Defined ID.
Tick the grade items to include.
Export to CSV or Excel.
grades.enter.other.export.verify: Open the file and confirm the learner count matches the Classlist total.
gotchas: Always start an import from an export. Hand-built files are the usual cause of failed imports.
The export reflects current visibility settings, so hidden items may not appear.
tickets: "I need to send final grades to the registrar."

grades.enter.other.recalculate.title: Recalculate final grades
grades.enter.other.recalculate.what: Forces D2L to work the final grades out again from current scores.
grades.enter.other.recalculate.when: A score changed but the final did not move, usually because automatic updating is switched off.
grades.enter.other.recalculate.learnerSees: An updated final grade, if theirs is released.
howTo: Open Grades > Enter Grades.
Click Recalculate.
Check the learner whose grade looked stale.
grades.enter.other.recalculate.verify: Compare the Final Calculated Grade against the individual item scores for one learner.
gotchas: Recalculating does not touch adjusted final grades. If the course releases the adjusted grade, this will not change what learners see.
tickets: "The final grade column is out of date."

grades.enter.other.transfer-calculated-a.title: Transfer calculated to adjusted
grades.enter.other.transfer-calculated-a.what: Copies every learner's calculated final into the adjusted column, giving the professor a starting point to edit by hand.
grades.enter.other.transfer-calculated-a.when: The course releases the adjusted final grade and the professor is about to curve or round.
grades.enter.other.transfer-calculated-a.learnerSees: Nothing until the adjusted grades are released.
howTo: Set Final Grade Released to Adjusted Final Grade first.
Open Grades > Enter Grades.
Click Transfer calculated to adjusted.
Edit the individual learners who need it, then save.
grades.enter.other.transfer-calculated-a.verify: Check that the adjusted column is populated and matches the calculated column before any edits.
gotchas: Running this again overwrites hand-made adjustments. Do it once, then edit.
Adjusted grades never update themselves afterwards.
tickets: "I want to round everyone up by two points."

grades.enter.other.released.title: Released
grades.enter.other.released.where: Grades > Enter Grades > Final Calculated Grade column
grades.enter.other.released.what: Ticking Released lets that learner see their final grade. It does not change the number at all.
grades.enter.other.released.when: The professor is ready for learners to see where they stand.
grades.enter.other.released.learnerSees: Their final grade appears. Until this is ticked, they see their individual item scores but no final.
howTo: Open Grades > Enter Grades.
Open View Actions for Final Calculated Grade, then Enter Grades.
Tick Released for the learners concerned, or use Final Grades > Release All.
Click Save.
grades.enter.other.released.verify: Open the learner view and confirm the final grade is visible.
gotchas: This is the single most common cause of 'the student cannot see their grade'. Check it before anything else.
Releasing is per learner, so a partially released class is normal and easy to miss.
tickets: "My student sees assignment scores but no final grade."
"Only some of my students can see their final grade."

grades.enter.other.switch-to-spreadsheet.title: Switch to Spreadsheet View
grades.enter.other.switch-to-spreadsheet.what: Swaps the grid for an editable spreadsheet-style view so the professor can type many grades quickly without opening each item.
grades.enter.other.switch-to-spreadsheet.when: Entering marks for a whole class in one sitting.
grades.enter.other.switch-to-spreadsheet.learnerSees: Nothing. It is a view for the professor only.
howTo: Open Grades > Enter Grades.
Click Switch to Spreadsheet View.
Type the grades, then Save.
grades.enter.other.switch-to-spreadsheet.verify: Switch back to the standard view and confirm the entered grades are there.
gotchas: Unsaved edits are lost when switching views. Save first.
Not modelled in this simulator; the button is here so the layout matches the real page.
tickets: "Is there a faster way to type in all these grades?"

grades.enter.other.open-learner-view.title: Open learner view
grades.enter.other.open-learner-view.what: Shows the gradebook as a learner sees it, which is how you confirm a visibility or release problem rather than guessing at it.
grades.enter.other.open-learner-view.when: Any ticket of the form 'my student cannot see X'. Check this before changing any setting.
howTo: Open Grades > Enter Grades.
Click Open learner view.
Compare what is visible against what the professor expects.
grades.enter.other.open-learner-view.verify: If the item is missing here, the cause is release, item visibility, or a date restriction.
gotchas: In real D2L, Preview does not apply special access or accommodations, so it is not a reliable way to test those. Impersonation is.
tickets: "The student says the grade is not there but I can see it."

grades.manage.other.bulk-edit.title: Bulk Edit
grades.manage.other.bulk-edit.what: Edits the properties of many grade items at once, such as names, max points, weights and short names, on a single page.
grades.manage.other.bulk-edit.when: Setting up a gradebook, or fixing weights across a whole course after a syllabus change.
grades.manage.other.bulk-edit.learnerSees: Whatever the edits change, such as renamed items or different point totals.
howTo: Open Grades > Manage Grades.
Click Bulk Edit.
Change the fields you need across all items.
Click Save.
grades.manage.other.bulk-edit.verify: Return to Manage Grades and confirm the weights total 100 if the course is weighted.
gotchas: Changing Max. Points after grades are entered rescales what those grades mean; the stored score does not move with it.
tickets: "I need to change the points on all my quizzes."

grades.manage.other.final-calculated-gra.title: Final Calculated Grade
grades.manage.other.final-calculated-gra.what: The course total D2L works out from every grade item according to the grading system. It is a row in Manage Grades, not an item anyone marks.
grades.manage.other.final-calculated-gra.when: Checking how the course total is built, or where its display and release settings live.
grades.manage.other.final-calculated-gra.learnerSees: This grade only once it is released to them.
howTo: Open Grades > Manage Grades.
Click Final Calculated Grade to see its properties and restrictions.
grades.manage.other.final-calculated-gra.verify: Its value for a learner should match a hand calculation from their item scores.
gotchas: Hiding this row hides the final grade from learners even when it is released.
tickets: "Where does the course total come from?"

grades.finals.other.final-adjusted-grade.title: Final Adjusted Grade
grades.finals.other.final-adjusted-grade.what: A final grade the professor can type over, sitting beside the calculated one. It only reaches learners if the course is set to release the adjusted grade.
grades.finals.other.final-adjusted-grade.when: Curving, rounding, or honouring an arrangement the gradebook cannot express.
grades.finals.other.final-adjusted-grade.learnerSees: This number instead of the calculated one, when the course releases adjusted grades and the learner's is released.
howTo: Set Final Grade Released to Adjusted Final Grade in Calculation Options.
Use Transfer calculated to adjusted to seed the column.
Edit the learners who need it and save.
grades.finals.other.final-adjusted-grade.verify: Check one edited learner in the learner view and confirm they see the adjusted number.
gotchas: It never recalculates. A later score fix will not reach it.
tickets: "I curved the grades but the students see the old numbers."

grades.display.other.display-how-final-g.title: Display how the final grade was calculated to users
grades.display.other.display-how-final-g.where: Grades > Settings > Org Unit Display Options
grades.display.other.display-how-final-g.what: Lets learners open a breakdown showing how their final grade was reached, item by item.
grades.display.other.display-how-final-g.when: The professor wants to cut down on 'how did you get this number' emails.
grades.display.other.display-how-final-g.learnerSees: A link in their grades that expands the calculation.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Org Unit Display Options.
Tick the option to display how the final grade was calculated.
Click Save.
grades.display.other.display-how-final-g.verify: Open the learner view and confirm the breakdown is reachable.
gotchas: It exposes weights and drops. If the professor is quietly dropping a low score, they may not want this on.
tickets: "Students keep asking me how their grade was worked out."

grades.schemes.other.new-scheme.title: New Scheme
grades.schemes.other.new-scheme.what: Creates a grade scheme: the ranges that turn a percentage into a letter or label, such as 93 and above being an A.
grades.schemes.other.new-scheme.when: The course reports letter grades, or the professor wants a custom set of bands.
grades.schemes.other.new-scheme.learnerSees: The letter or label instead of, or alongside, the percentage, depending on the display options.
howTo: Open Grades, then the Schemes tab.
Click New Scheme and name it.
Add each range with its start percentage, symbol and assigned value.
Save, then set it on the items or as the course default.
grades.schemes.other.new-scheme.verify: Check a learner at a boundary percentage falls in the band the professor expects.
gotchas: Ranges must not leave gaps, or a learner can land between bands.
A scheme has to be attached to an item or set as default before it does anything.
tickets: "I want letter grades instead of percentages."

grades.schemes.other.default-scheme-perc.title: Default Scheme
grades.schemes.other.default-scheme-perc.what: The scheme applied to any grade item that does not choose its own, and to the final grade.
grades.schemes.other.default-scheme-perc.when: Setting a course up so every item reports the same way without setting each one individually.
grades.schemes.other.default-scheme-perc.learnerSees: Their grades expressed through this scheme.
howTo: Open Grades, then the Schemes tab.
Choose the scheme from the Default Scheme list.
Click Save default scheme.
grades.schemes.other.default-scheme-perc.verify: Open a grade item that has no scheme of its own and confirm it now reports through this one.
gotchas: Changing the default re-labels existing grades immediately across the course.
tickets: "All my quizzes are showing percentages, not letters."

grades.finals.other.release-final-calcul.title: Release Final Calculated Grade to a learner
grades.finals.other.release-final-calcul.what: Releases one named learner's final grade so they can see it. Releasing is per learner, which is why a class can end up half able to see their grade and half not.
grades.finals.other.release-final-calcul.when: A single learner asks why they cannot see a final grade everyone else can see.
grades.finals.other.release-final-calcul.learnerSees: Their final grade appears in Grades. Until then they see item scores but no course total.
howTo: Open Grades, then the Final Grades tab.
Find the learner.
Tick Release for that learner, or use Final Grades > Release All for the whole class.
Click Save.
grades.finals.other.release-final-calcul.verify: Open the learner view for that learner and confirm the final grade is now visible.
gotchas: Release does not change the number, only who can see it.
Release All covers current enrolments. A learner added later starts unreleased.
tickets: "One student says they cannot see their final grade but everyone else can."

grades.personal.other.grade-scheme-symbo.title: Show the grade scheme symbol
grades.personal.other.grade-scheme-symbo.what: Adds the scheme's label, such as A- or Satisfactory, to what is shown in the gradebook alongside or instead of the raw number.
grades.personal.other.grade-scheme-symbo.when: The course reports letter grades and the professor wants to see them while marking.
grades.personal.other.grade-scheme-symbo.learnerSees: Nothing from this setting. Personal Display Options change the professor's own view only; the learner's view is governed by Org Unit Display Options.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Personal Display Options.
Tick Grade scheme symbol.
Click Save.
grades.personal.other.grade-scheme-symbo.verify: Return to Enter Grades and confirm the letter appears next to the scores.
gotchas: Professors often change this expecting learners to see the difference. Point them at Org Unit Display Options instead.
Nothing shows unless a scheme is attached to the item or set as the course default.
tickets: "I turned on letter grades but my students still see percentages."

grades.personal.other.org-defined-id.title: Show Org Defined ID
grades.personal.other.org-defined-id.where: Grades > Settings > Personal Display Options > User Details
grades.personal.other.org-defined-id.what: Adds the institutional student identifier as a column in the professor's gradebook view.
grades.personal.other.org-defined-id.when: Reconciling grades against a spreadsheet or the registrar, where names are ambiguous and IDs are not.
grades.personal.other.org-defined-id.learnerSees: Nothing. This is a professor-side display setting.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Personal Display Options.
Tick Org Defined ID under User Details.
Click Save.
grades.personal.other.org-defined-id.verify: Enter Grades should now show the ID column beside learner names.
gotchas: Org Defined ID is what grade imports match on, so this is worth turning on before diagnosing a failed import.
Two learners can share a name; they do not share an Org Defined ID.
tickets: "My grade import matched the wrong students."
"I have two students with the same name."

grades.wizard.other.start.title: Start the Grades Setup Wizard
grades.wizard.other.start.what: Walks a professor through the gradebook decisions in order: grading system, release, ungraded items, decimals and default scheme. It sets the same options as the Settings tabs, just in a guided sequence.
grades.wizard.other.start.when: A brand new course, or a professor who does not know which settings matter.
grades.wizard.other.start.learnerSees: Nothing directly, but the choices made here decide what appears in their grades.
howTo: Open Grades, then Setup Wizard.
Click Start.
Work through each step, reading the summary at the end before finishing.
grades.wizard.other.start.verify: The final step shows a summary of every choice. Check it against the syllabus before the professor commits.
gotchas: Re-running the wizard on a live course rewrites settings that already have grades behind them, which moves every final grade.
It does not create grade items; it only configures how they add up.
tickets: "I am setting up a new course, where do I start with grades?"

grades.manage.other.view-event-log.title: View Event Log
grades.manage.other.view-event-log.where: Grades > Manage Grades > More Actions > View Event Log
grades.manage.other.view-event-log.what: A record of changes to the gradebook: who changed a grade, when, and in some cases the chance to restore a deleted grade item.
grades.manage.other.view-event-log.when: A professor says a grade or column changed and they did not do it, or something was deleted by accident.
grades.manage.other.view-event-log.learnerSees: Nothing. The log is staff-side only.
howTo: Open Grades, then Manage Grades.
Click More Actions, then View Event Log.
Find the entry by date and item, and use Restore if it is offered.
grades.manage.other.view-event-log.verify: After a restore, confirm the item is back in Manage Grades with its grades intact.
gotchas: Restore is not offered for every item type, and not forever. Treat an accidental delete as urgent.
The log shows changes, not intentions: a grade changing may simply be a recalculation.
tickets: "I deleted a grade column by mistake, can I get it back?"
"A student's grade changed and I did not change it."

grades.manage.other.edit-categories.title: Edit Categories
grades.manage.other.edit-categories.where: Toolbar of Assignments, Quizzes and similar tools
grades.manage.other.edit-categories.what: Manages the categories that group items inside a tool, for tidying a long list. These are not gradebook categories and carry no weight.
grades.manage.other.edit-categories.when: A professor wants their quiz or assignment list organised into sections.
grades.manage.other.edit-categories.learnerSees: Items grouped under headings in the tool's list.
howTo: Click Edit Categories in the tool's toolbar.
Add, rename or remove categories.
Save, then set each item's category when editing it.
grades.manage.other.edit-categories.verify: The list shows items grouped under their categories.
gotchas: Easily confused with a Grades category, which does affect weighting. A tool category is presentation only.
tickets: "How do I group my quizzes by unit?"

grades.personal.other.points-grade.title: Show the points grade (your view)
grades.personal.other.points-grade.where: Grades > Settings > Personal Display Options > Grade Details
grades.personal.other.points-grade.what: Shows raw points, such as 18/20, in the gradebook as you see it while marking.
grades.personal.other.points-grade.when: You are checking marks and want the underlying points rather than a percentage.
grades.personal.other.points-grade.learnerSees: Nothing. Personal Display Options change only your own view.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Personal Display Options.
Tick Points grade.
Click Save.
grades.personal.other.points-grade.verify: Enter Grades should now show points beside or instead of percentages.
gotchas: Professors routinely change this and expect learners to see the difference. The learner-facing equivalent is in Org Unit Display Options.
tickets: "I turned on points but my students still see percentages."

grades.display.other.points-grade.title: Show the points grade (learner view)
grades.display.other.points-grade.where: Grades > Settings > Org Unit Display Options > Student View Display Options
grades.display.other.points-grade.what: Shows learners their raw points, such as 18/20, in their own grades page.
grades.display.other.points-grade.when: The professor wants learners to see points rather than, or as well as, a percentage.
grades.display.other.points-grade.learnerSees: Points on each item, exactly as configured here.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Org Unit Display Options.
Tick Points grade under the student view options.
Click Save.
grades.display.other.points-grade.verify: Open the learner view and confirm points appear.
gotchas: This is the setting professors actually want when they ask about what students see. Personal Display Options only changes their own view.
tickets: "My students cannot see how many points they got."

grades.display.other.weighted-grade.title: Show the weighted grade (learner view)
grades.display.other.weighted-grade.where: Grades > Settings > Org Unit Display Options > Student View Display Options
grades.display.other.weighted-grade.what: Shows learners each item's contribution as a weighted percentage of the course, rather than only its own score.
grades.display.other.weighted-grade.when: A weighted course where learners keep asking how much an item is really worth.
grades.display.other.weighted-grade.learnerSees: The weighted contribution beside each item.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Org Unit Display Options.
Tick Weighted grade under the student view options.
Click Save.
grades.display.other.weighted-grade.verify: Open the learner view and confirm the weighted figures appear.
gotchas: Only meaningful when the grading system is Weighted. In a Points course it will confuse more than it explains.

grades.personal.other.grade-scheme-color.title: Show the grade scheme colour
grades.personal.other.grade-scheme-color.what: Shades grades with the colour set on the scheme's ranges, so a gradebook can be scanned at a glance.
grades.personal.other.grade-scheme-color.when: Looking for learners in trouble across a large class.
grades.personal.other.grade-scheme-color.learnerSees: Nothing from this setting; it changes your own view only.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Personal Display Options.
Tick Grade scheme color.
Click Save.
grades.personal.other.grade-scheme-color.verify: Grades should now carry the scheme's colours in Enter Grades.
gotchas: Nothing happens unless the scheme's ranges actually have colours set.
Colour alone should never be the only signal; it fails for colour-blind users and in print.

grades.personal.other.username.title: Show Username
grades.personal.other.username.where: Grades > Settings > Personal Display Options > User Details
grades.personal.other.username.what: Adds the learner's D2L username as a column in your gradebook view.
grades.personal.other.username.when: Matching learners against another system, or telling apart two people with the same name.
grades.personal.other.username.learnerSees: Nothing. This is a staff-side display setting.
howTo: Open Grades, then Settings, then Personal Display Options.
Tick Username under User Details.
Click Save.
grades.personal.other.username.verify: Enter Grades shows the username column.
gotchas: Grade imports can match on username or Org Defined ID. Check which the file uses before importing.
